title: Origin-destination data explorer: Census 2021
meta_description: A tool to view animated flows of people moving between places for work or migration, based on data from Census 2021, to a neighbourhood (MSOA) level. Choose between visualised flows for Migration flows (Movement from address 12 months prior to census day) and Workplace flows (Usual residence and place of work).
lede: A tool to show animated flows of people for travel to work or migration, based on Census 2021.

body.text: This is an [interactive guide and tool](/visualisations/censusorigindestination/) for exploring some of the origin-destination data published for Census 2021.
Origin-destination data show the movement of people from one location to another, such as migration and commuting patterns. It is sometimes known as "flow data".
The coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic strongly affected patterns of population movement. Census day was 21 March 2021, when lockdown restrictions were in force in the UK.
Use our interactive tool to visualise population flows
Migration flows - Movement from address 12 months prior to census day
Workplace flows - Usual residence and place of work
You can also switch direction to see aggregated movements to and from an area.
The tool is also embeddable for use in external websites. A link is provided within the guide article.

You can [download the data used in this tool](https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/sources/census_2021_od), along with a wider range of origin-destination datasets, from Nomis. You can read more about these datasets and how to use them in the [User guide to Census 2021 origin-destination data](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationestimates/methodologies/userguidetocensus2021origindestinationdataenglandandwales). Main findings about this data can be found in the [origin-destination data bulletin](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationestimates/bulletins/origindestinationdataenglandandwales/census2021).
